title: Agenda safety
description: Majority voting on an agenda is always consistent exactly if every minimally inconsistent subset has at most two formulas; checking this is Pi-2-complete (Endriss, Grandi and Porello). The solutions are the witnesses of unsafety: the abstraction guesses a subset of three or more formulas with, for each member, a model of the others, and the check looks for a model of the whole subset. The sample is the agenda of the doctrinal paradox.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The agenda, as formulas in clause form. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.
formula(F) :- cl(F,_).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): subsets of three or more formulas, each proper subset of which is consistent.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: at least three formulas of the agenda ...
3 { in(F) : formula(F) }.
% ... such that leaving out any one of them gives a consistent set: for each chosen F,
% w(F,V) is a model of the other chosen formulas. These models are private to solver A.
{ w(F,V) } :- in(F), var(V).
:- in(F), in(G), F != G, cl(G,C), not w(F,V) : pos(C,V); w(F,V) : neg(C,V).
#show in/1.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the chosen formulas.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a model of all chosen formulas (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: a model of all chosen formulas. Then the subset is consistent.
{ m(V) } :- var(V).
false(F) :- cl(F,C), not m(V) : pos(C,V); m(V) : neg(C,V).
:- in(F), false(F).
#show m/1.

% The model satisfies every subset of the formulas that are true in it. So a formula
% that is false in it has to be chosen. (There always is one: the agenda contains the
% negation of each formula.)
relevant(in(F)) :- formula(F), false(F).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.clause(M, X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

library.summary: Minimally inconsistent subsets of an agenda with three or more formulas, the witnesses that majority voting is unsafe (doctrinal paradox agenda, 6 solutions).

instances.facts:
% An agenda for judgment aggregation: the premises p and q, the conclusion r, the
% doctrine "r holds exactly if p and q hold", and the negation of each.
% cl(F,C): clause C belongs to formula F; pos(C,V) / neg(C,V): its literals.
var(p;q;r).
cl(p,1).   pos(1,p).                              % p
cl(np,2).  neg(2,p).                              % not p
cl(q,3).   pos(3,q).                              % q
cl(nq,4).  neg(4,q).                              % not q
cl(r,5).   pos(5,r).                              % r
cl(nr,6).  neg(6,r).                              % not r
cl(d,7).   neg(7,r). pos(7,p).                    % doctrine: r implies p,
cl(d,8).   neg(8,r). pos(8,q).                    %           r implies q,
cl(d,9).   pos(9,r). neg(9,p). neg(9,q).          %           p and q imply r
cl(nd,10). pos(10,r). pos(10,p).                  % its negation: r or p,
cl(nd,11). pos(11,r). pos(11,q).                  %               r or q,
cl(nd,12). neg(12,r). neg(12,p). neg(12,q).       %               not all three

% Only two independent premises and their negations: every inconsistent subset
% is a premise with its negation, so none has three formulas.
var(p;q).
cl(p,1).   pos(1,p).                              % p
cl(np,2).  neg(2,p).                              % not p
cl(q,3).   pos(3,q).                              % q
cl(nq,4).  neg(4,q).                              % not q

% The premises p and q, the conclusion r, the rule "r holds exactly if p or q
% holds", and the negation of each.
var(p;q;r).
cl(p,1).   pos(1,p).                              % p
cl(np,2).  neg(2,p).                              % not p
cl(q,3).   pos(3,q).                              % q
cl(nq,4).  neg(4,q).                              % not q
cl(r,5).   pos(5,r).                              % r
cl(nr,6).  neg(6,r).                              % not r
cl(d,7).   neg(7,r). pos(7,p). pos(7,q).          % rule: r implies p or q,
cl(d,8).   neg(8,p). pos(8,r).                    %       p implies r,
cl(d,9).   neg(9,q). pos(9,r).                    %       q implies r
cl(nd,10). pos(10,r). pos(10,p). pos(10,q).       % its negation: r or p or q,
cl(nd,11). neg(11,r). neg(11,p).                  %   not both r and p,
cl(nd,12). neg(12,r). neg(12,q).                  %   not both r and q
